definitions.explanation: The look and feel of a material or surface — how something feels to the touch or appears in terms of material quality. Commonly used in fashion, design, and product descriptions.

examples.japanese: この{革|かわ}は{質感|しつかん}がいい。
examples.english: This leather has a nice texture.

examples.japanese: {高級|こうきゅう}な{質感|しつかん}の{生地|きじ}を{使|つか}っている。
examples.english: It uses fabric with a luxurious feel.

examples.japanese: この{塗料|とりょう}を{使|つか}えば、{木|き}の{質感|しつかん}を{活|い}かした{仕上|しあ}がりになる。
examples.english: Using this paint will give a finish that brings out the texture of the wood.

notes:
{質感|しつかん} describes the tactile or visual quality of a material — how it feels to the touch or looks in terms of texture and substance.

ETYMOLOGY:
Combines {質|しつ} (quality, substance) + {感|かん} (feeling, sensation).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {質感|しつかん}がいい: has a nice texture/feel
- {質感|しつかん}が{高|たか}い: feels high-quality
- {質感|しつかん}を{活|い}かす: to bring out the texture
- {質感|しつかん}のある: having good texture

DOMAINS:
Frequently used in fashion, interior design, product reviews, and visual arts. In CG graphics and photography, it refers to how realistic a surface appears.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {手触|てざわ}り: how something feels to the touch (purely tactile)
- {肌触|はだざわ}り: feel against the skin (fabric, sheets)
